item.text:
`Simulator` is now much narrower. I extracted setup and seeding into [`SimulationFactory.java`](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R008_module_java/SimulationFactory.java:11), which now owns:

- dimension normalization and default sizing
- `Time` / `Weather` / `Field` / `SimulatorView` creation
- control button creation
- view color registration
- initial field population

The factory returns a bundled runtime via [`SimulationComponents`](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R008_module_java/SimulationFactory.java:263) and named buttons via [`SimulationButtons`](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R008_module_java/SimulationFactory.java:204). `Simulator` now just wires those in through [`initializeSimulation(...)`](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R008_module_java/Simulator.java:172) and delegates reset seeding to [`simulationFactory.populate(...)`](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R008_module_java/Simulator.java:163).

That leaves [`Simulator.java`](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R008_module_java/Simulator.java:12) focused on simulation control: stepping, pause/play state, reset flow, and organism advancement. The previous constructor/setup clutter, UI bootstrapping, and random population logic are gone from the entry point.

Verification: `javac *.java` succeeds.
